title: Received practice: salute, kiss, kneel, offer incense and lights; set images on altars; process, vow, gift, and pilgrimage to them
source_text: XVII. Talis est non solum consuetudo imagines Christi & Sanctorum salutandi, osculandi, & genu coram eis flectendi, ac etiam suffitus & luminaria ipsis offerendi, quae, ut modo vidimus, expresse probant Ecclesiae Romanae Concilia; sed praeterea mos ille receptus, quo imagines super altaribus locantur, vestibus & monilibus pretiosis ornantur, solenni pompa per vias publicas circumferuntur, vota eis nuncupantur, donaria consecrantur, & religiosae peregrinationes ad eas suscipiuntur.
pass_a_gloss: Such is not only the custom of saluting, kissing, and bending the knee before the images of Christ and of the Saints, and also of offering them incense and lights, which, as we have just seen, the Councils of the Roman Church expressly approve; but besides that received usage by which images are placed upon altars, are adorned with precious garments and necklaces, are carried about by solemn pomp through the public streets, vows are vowed to them, gifts are consecrated, and religious pilgrimages are undertaken to them.
pass_b_english: Beyond Council-approved kiss and kneel come altar-placement, rich adornment, street processions, vows, offerings, and pilgrimages to images.

choices.why: Shows practice pressing past ‘relative honor’ language.
